## 8. Models

<!-- models:start (generated by tools/process_models.mjs; edit outside these markers) -->

### Slit-scan (`lumenary:slit-scan`, models this process)

_From: Photo-finish cameras and special effects; when: Finish-line cameras from the 1940s; the stargate of 2001 in 1968; works best on: Video with a clear direction of movement; bold still pictures._

An ordinary camera takes the whole frame at one instant. A slit camera looks through a gap a few pixels wide and records that strip over and over as time passes, laying the strips side by side. Whatever is still piles up into stripes, whatever moves is drawn as its own shape, and a runner crossing the line is drawn as an outline of time. When the slit also moves across a still picture, the picture stretches wherever the slit slows down.

**How it is made, as the model does it:**

1. Choose a narrow slit of the frame: a single column or row.
2. At a steady rate, copy that slit into a strip that scrolls away, so that the newest slit enters at one edge.
3. For the time warp, keep a ring of recent frames and take each row from a different age of it.
4. On a still picture, sweep the slit across it and back, or shear the frames, so that there is something to scan.
5. Read between two neighbouring columns, so the strip stays smooth.

**The maths:**

$$s(t)=c+A\,\frac{\arcsin\!\big(0.92\,\sin(\omega(t-t_0)+1.3)\big)}{\arcsin 0.92}$$

_The slit swept across a still picture: a triangle wave with rounded ends, where A is 0.46 of the picture._ (written for this model: specific)

$$\Delta u=\frac{v}{r}$$

_Picture pixels per strip line: v is the slit’s speed across the picture and r the scroll rate. Below 1 the picture is stretched, above 1 squeezed, and with a negative sign mirrored._ (written for this model: specific)

$$C(x,y)=(1-\phi)\,F_{a}(x,y)+\phi\,F_{a+1}(x,y),\qquad a+\phi=f(x,y)\,(K-1)$$

_The time warp: F_a is the frame a steps back and f the lag, from 0 to 1._ (primitives: frame-history)

**Dials:** `mode` (Kind of scan) = "finish" (finish, warp); `speed` (Scroll speed (finish line)) = 45 [10 to 100]; `slit` (Where the slit is (finish line)) = 50 [5 to 95]; `way` (Scrolls towards (finish line)) = "left" (left, right, up, down); `spread` (Time spread (time warp)) = 55 [10 to 100]; `shape` (Warp shape (time warp)) = "down" (down, across, ripple, tunnel).

**History:** The slit camera was first used to settle photo finishes at race tracks in the 1940s: film moved past a slit aimed at the finish line, so the picture showed who crossed first, with time running along the film. In 1968 Douglas Trumbull used a much larger version to make the psychedelic stargate corridor in 2001: A Space Odyssey, moving artwork past a slit while the camera shutter stayed open. The same trick is now a standard video effect, and finish-line cameras record thousands of lines a second.
